answer: A farm faking 566 aliases needs 566 separate verifiable records of this kind, each checked against the issuing authority, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. The seat is earned with weather station observer log: readings logged at one station across years of skies. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The violet record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the vine entry is checkable by anyone, and the umber window closes before a farm can catch up.
